definition: Cognitive computing refers to technology platforms that, broadly speaking, are based on the scientific disciplines of artificial intelligence and signal processing.
details: These platforms encompass machine learning, reasoning, natural language processing, speech recognition and vision (object recognition), human–computer interaction, dialog and narrative generation, among other technologies.

explainer.lead: Cognitive computing is a broad label for platforms that combine artificial intelligence and signal processing to work with speech, images, language, and human interaction. It matters because these capabilities can be connected so a system can interpret different kinds of input and produce a useful response.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a computer that can listen, look, think about what it noticed, and answer you, a bit like a helpful friend using their ears, eyes, and brain. Cognitive computing is the idea of building computer systems from tools that do these jobs. It is not one single invention, but a way of bringing several abilities together.
tiers.practitioner: In practice, a platform may combine signal processing and machine learning with components for speech recognition, object recognition, natural language processing, reasoning, and dialogue generation. The main design task is connecting these components so their outputs can inform interpretation, interaction, and responses. Because the term is broad, it does not by itself specify an architecture, model, or evaluation method.
tiers.paperLevel: Cognitive computing denotes technology platforms based broadly on artificial intelligence and signal processing. Their capabilities can include machine learning, reasoning, natural language processing, speech and object recognition, human–computer interaction, and dialogue and narrative generation; the term does not define a single formal algorithm or fixed platform structure.

explainer.example: A user shows a system a photograph of a bicycle and asks, “What is this?”: vision recognizes the bicycle, speech recognition and language processing interpret the question, and dialogue generation produces the answer, “That is a bicycle.”

usedIn.name: Voice interfaces
usedIn.detail: Speech recognition, language processing, and dialogue generation can turn a spoken request into a spoken or written response.

usedIn.name: Visual recognition systems
usedIn.detail: Object recognition can identify items in images and supply information to other parts of a platform.

usedIn.name: Interactive dialogue systems
usedIn.detail: Language processing, reasoning, and dialogue generation can support exchanges between people and computers.

explainer.intuition: The idea is to combine capabilities for sensing, interpreting, reasoning, and communicating rather than treating each as an isolated feature. Signal processing and AI techniques handle inputs such as speech and images, while language and interaction components help the platform respond to people.
howItWorks: Receive input such as speech, images, or text.
Process signals and recognize features, words, or objects.
Interpret the request using language processing and reasoning.
Generate a response through dialogue, narrative, or another interface.
explainer.whyItMatters: It provides a way to describe platforms that bring perception, language, reasoning, and interaction together. That combination can support richer exchanges with computers than any one capability provides alone.
misconceptions: It is not a single algorithm; it is a broad platform concept.
It is not limited to machine learning and can also include reasoning, recognition, and interaction.
Recognizing speech or objects alone does not make a complete cognitive computing platform.

nodes.label: Human input
nodes.note: Speech, images, or text enter the platform.

nodes.label: Language and reasoning
nodes.note: Interprets input and determines a response.

nodes.label: Human interaction
nodes.note: Presents the response through an interface.
